claims.text: Short-range ordering is the primary control on the high-temperature mechanical strength and thermoelastic modulus of equiatomic MoNbTaW.
Short-range ordering increases local lattice distortion in equiatomic MoNbTaW.
Short-range ordering increases lattice friction stress in equiatomic MoNbTaW.
Direct water quenching from 1200 °C produces a relatively low-SRO MoNbTaW baseline.
Annealing MoNbTaW at 800 °C for 100 h followed by water quenching produces a relatively high-SRO state.
The relevant structural mediator consists of short-range ordered clusters among Mo, Nb, Ta, and W atoms in a BCC lattice.
SRO-induced local lattice distortions raise the shear modulus.
SRO-induced local lattice distortions raise lattice friction stress.
The increased lattice friction stress impedes dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases the high-temperature yield strength.
The high-SRO alloy will have approximately 10% higher Young's modulus at 900 °C than the low-SRO baseline.
The high-SRO alloy will have approximately 50 MPa higher yield strength at 900 °C than the low-SRO baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase BCC MoNbTaW from 600 °C to 1000 °C at strain rates from 1×10^-4 to 1×10^-2 s^-1 when significant carbide or oxide precipitation is absent.
SRO kinetics and competing precipitation at high temperature may alter the magnitude of the predicted effects.
